requirements.requirement: Every command run through sudo on node1 is recorded with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
requirements.summary: A sudoers.d drop-in (00-sudo-logging) sets Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log" with log_year and log_host enabled. Test commands (whoami, id) produced correctly formatted entries with timestamp, user=root, HOST, PWD, and COMMAND fields, both before and after a full node restart, confirming persistence of the logging behavior.

requirements.requirement: Sudo log entries are kept out of the general system log (/var/log/messages via busybox syslogd)
requirements.summary: Defaults !syslog was added to the sudoers.d drop-in. After running sudo commands, grep of /var/log/messages showed only pre-existing sudo entries dated before the config change, with no new sudo-related lines appended — verified both immediately after configuration and again after the reboot.

requirements.requirement: Restart evidence protocol: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered configuration/functional state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (39963d5e...) and healthy config/log state were captured, a backgrounded reboot command returned an acknowledgement before disconnect, repeated polling through connection failures confirmed the node was down, and a new boot_id (16b634f5...) was observed on reconnect — matching the fixed global boot-identity snapshots. Post-restart checks confirmed the sudoers.d file intact, visudo -c clean, syslogd running, and new sudo commands correctly logged to the dedicated file with no new /var/log/messages entries.

overall_summary: The executor correctly configured sudo on node1 to log every invocation (user, timestamp, host, PWD, command) to /var/log/sudo-commands.log via a sudoers.d drop-in using 'Defaults logfile=...' plus log_year/log_host, and disabled sudo's syslog output with 'Defaults !syslog', verified by direct before/after greps of /var/log/messages showing no new sudo entries. The provider-wide restart evidence protocol was also executed cleanly: pre-restart boot identity and healthy state, a reboot acknowledgement, a distinct post-restart boot identity, and full functional recovery of the logging configuration were all directly observed and cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: Two small temporary files (/tmp/sudo-logging, /tmp/reboot.log) were left on node1 after the task rather than being cleaned up; this is minor residue with no functional or security impact.

The post-reboot 'sudo hostname' output showed a different-looking hostname string (vm-rhel8-...) than the pre-reboot HOST field (node1) in log entries; this appears to be an artifact of the underlying platform/VM naming layer unrelated to the sudo logging configuration and was not further investigated.

operational_hygiene.summary: Almost all executor commands were either read-only discovery/verification or directly necessary to satisfy the task (installing the sudoers.d drop-in, creating/permissioning the log file, running test sudo commands to validate behavior, and performing the required restart evidence sequence). The only hygiene gap is that two temporary files created during the work — /tmp/sudo-logging (the staging copy of the sudoers drop-in, from cmd-744434011db745ce) and /tmp/reboot.log (redirection target for the backgrounded reboot, from cmd-d9e2d53d68cd4ea1) — were left behind and appear in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot rather than being cleaned up. These are small, non-sensitive, non-executable residue files with no functional impact, so the deduction is modest.
